summary: This regulation explains the rules for independent directors on the board of a listed company. It covers how they are appointed, their meetings, their responsibilities, and how they must give a yearly declaration of independence. Companies must also help them learn about the business and sometimes buy insurance for them.
points: The listed entity must not appoint or keep an alternate director for an independent director.
The listed entity must get shareholder approval by a special resolution to appoint, re-appoint, or remove an independent director.
Independent directors must hold at least one yearly meeting without non-independent directors and management present.
The listed entity must run familiarisation programmes to teach independent directors about the industry, business model, and their roles.
The board of directors must take on record the independence declaration submitted by each independent director after checking it.
example: Green Energy Limited, a listed company, wanted to appoint Mr. Roy as an independent director. They put the proposal to a vote, and it was approved by shareholders through a special resolution. To help Mr. Roy understand his new role, Green Energy Limited conducted a familiarisation programme explaining their business model and industry. Later, the independent directors held a yearly meeting without any management members present to review the performance of the board. Mr. Roy also submitted a formal declaration at the first board meeting of the financial year stating that he meets all the criteria to act as an independent director.

terms.meaning: A board member who is independent of company management and does not have a material or pecuniary relationship with the company.
A formal decision passed by shareholders with a high majority of votes.
A person appointed to act for a director during their absence.
The total market value of a company's issued shares.

watch: An independent director can still be appointed even if a special resolution fails, as long as specific voting conditions involving public shareholders are met.
